---
title: "Set up"
subtitle: "What you need, and how to check it works"
---

```{=html}
<div class="stepmeta"><b>You need</b><span>R 4.1 or later. Nothing else for the modelling.</span><b>You get</b><span>the data in memory, and a quick test that the whole pipeline runs.</span></div>
```

## Get the files

```sh
git clone https://github.com/corne00/dynamic-gxe-workshop.git
cd dynamic-gxe-workshop
```

The folder has three parts you will use:

| Folder | Content |
|---|---|
| `R/functions.R` | every function in the workshop, plain base R |
| `data/` | the Narrabri weather, biomass trajectories and APSIM cultivar parameters |
| `scripts/` | a command-line version of the full pipeline |

## Packages

The modelling uses base R only. The plots use `ggplot2`:

```r
install.packages("ggplot2")
```

## Check that it works

```r
source("R/functions.R")

wx   <- read.csv("data/narrabri_weather.csv")        # daily weather
traj <- read.csv("data/narrabri_biomass.csv.gz")     # daily biomass, one row per genotype x year x day

drv   <- make_drivers(wx)
Theta <- make_library(drv)
tr    <- make_trajectories(traj, drv)
gram  <- gram_stats(Theta, tr)

cv <- cv_blocked(Theta, tr, gram, fit_ssr, k = 12)    # leave-one-year-out, 31 fits
round(evaluate(cv$pred, tr), 3)
```

You should see a trajectory RMSE of about 0.52 t/ha on years the model never saw. If you do, everything is in place.

::: {.callout-tip title="Check"}
The same numbers come out of the original research code (Python): trajectory RMSE 0.520, RMSE at day 113 of 0.688 and at maturity of 0.749 t/ha. The base-R version gives 0.521, 0.689 and 0.747.
:::
